correctness.rationale: The frozen proof incorrectly says that at either adherence boundary there is at most one feasible epidemiological equilibrium. For example, in the given family at x=0 both (1,0,0) and (1/2,5/18,0) exist. In the repair the disease-free equilibrium is always included, and the behavioral row at an adherence boundary yields a block triangular Jacobian. Whenever an endemic point exists the disease-free point has positive infection invasion eigenvalue, so at most one boundary hyperbolic sink remains possible. No disease-free interior point can be a sink, since its behavior eigenvalue is positive. For mixed endemic points with a>0 the reduced G is strictly concave. The endemic (S,I) block B is invertible with positive determinant, and the Schur complement in the full Jacobian is epsilon*x*(1-x)*G'(x), using the derivative of the endemic branch -B^(-1)*partial_x f. Thus a Hurwitz point must be a descending crossing, and strict concavity allows at most one; at a=0 any interior payoff root has positive behavioral eigenvalue. These facts support the credited background bound, not a claim that only three equilibria exist. In the repaired fixed family, the positive endemic branch is 0<=x<1/2. The endpoints of its payoff curve are 1/10-c and -c; its maximum at x_m=1-sqrt(5/8) is (7-2sqrt(10))/5-c. Inside the strict window there are two roots, the larger below 3/8. The lower has C3<0; the upper has C3>0 and is Hurwitz by uniform inequalities on [1/5,3/8], using C1>=169/180, C2>=3/40, C3<=3/80, so C1*C2-C3>=79/2400. Independent replay (python3 /workspace/branches/replay_exact_audit.py 4) derived all three coefficients from the full vector field and gave positive exact Bernstein minima 685/16, 1605/256 and 807825/4096 for the respective cleared polynomials, checked both boundary characteristic factors, and recovered 40x^2-16x+1 for c=3/25. At c<=1/10 the nonadherence boundary has no hyperbolic sink; at the upper endpoint the double mixed root has zero eigenvalue; above it no mixed endemic point exists. Full adherence is stable throughout the strict window since c<2/5. The disease-free interior saddle has two negative epidemic eigenvalues and a positive behavioral one. Strict stability, continuation on the invariant faces, and positive interior fractions at the mixed state give robustness within the admissible parameter set. The frozen checker was inspected, not run; its auxiliary radical comparisons are floating-point, as now described in the repair.
residual_risks: Strict Jacobian stability is a local equilibrium claim, not a global-basin, recurrent-attractor, or empirical result.

Its rational witness (a=e=1/2, epsilon=1/10) and open-neighborhood claim do not identify either end of the fixed-family cost interval at a=1,e=0,epsilon=1, or suffice for the stability inequalities throughout that interval. The initiating paper defines the model, gives qualitative multistability maps and the equivalent generic stability tests, not the explicit fixed-family iff interval in the passages inspected. Coverage is separated from priority: the comparator has a later catalogue path date and no priority conclusion follows.

checked_sources: Repaired RESULT.md, uniform Hurwitz proof and strict endpoint exclusions
value.rationale: The repaired contribution answers a meaningful parameter question left by an isolated coexistence witness: at fixed disease and payoff parameters, what exact range of the adherence cost allows all three local outcomes? The simplified protection corner makes the two different losses of coexistence analytically distinguishable, while strict stability shows this is not a degeneracy limited to zero source efficacy. The lower endpoint is set by the nonadherent equilibrium's transverse eigenvalue and the upper by merger of the mixed roots, with no untested extra instability along the upper branch. This complete cost classification is useful as a solvable benchmark and not an extrapolation to epidemic policy or equilibria outside the model.
residual_risks: Value is mathematical and local; costs and efficacies are not empirical calibrations and no global attractor theorem follows.
